newsitem.title: PERU: Peru TV image shows hostages inside residence.
newsitem.headline: Peru TV image shows hostages inside residence.

text.p: A Peruvian television station showed on Saturday a still photographic image of hostages inside the Japanese ambassador's residence held by Marxist rebels for four days.
The photograph showed at least seven men, most of whom appeared to be middle-aged, dressed in shirts and pants.
The national Channel 5 television station did not say when the still was taken nor how it was obtained.
Several hostages have been filmed appearing at various windows of the luxury mansion, but no other pictures have showed them on the interior.

Looking relaxed, some of the men were seated in armchairs, or on the floor and some were standing up, leaning against the wall of the single room presented in the image. One man walked past his companions, none of whom seemed to be talking to each other. One of the seated men was smoking a cigarette.
The room shown in the image had a carpeted floor, an open door and an electric fan in the corner.
None of the hostages in the photograph were immediatley identified.

Channel 5 said it would present more pictures later on Saturday including an image of Peruvian Foreign Minister Francisco Tudela, held since late Tuesday along with about 340 hostages by the Tupac Amaru Revolutionary Movement (MRTA) rebels.

The still was presented minutes after a rival television station established a walkie-talkie radio link MRTA rebels inside the home. They spoke for about 20 minutes to rebel leader Nestor Cerpa, Tudela and Japanese Ambassador Morihisa Aoki.
